Earn is a rolled-up prospect of 4 segments: Earn Central; Earn North; Earn South and Earn West. Common volumetric inputs for all segments are quoted above. Stochastic rolling-up of the Earn segments has been performed in two stages. First, Central, North and South segments were rolled-up with the North and South trap risk dependant on the Central segment. Reservoir thickness, NTG, porosity and gas saturation were all assigned a maximum positive correlation. GWC of the North segment was assigned a maximum positive correlation to the Central segment GWC based on the probability of fault communication between these segments. Secondly, the three rolled-up segments were then rolled up with the West segment, with no trap risk dependency applied, based on the assumption that the West segment trap is independent of the other three segments.

Volumetric calculation for basement has involved calculating the volume of a ca 16m to 25m carapace of weathered and fractured granite. This thickness of weathering zone at top basement was observed directly 205/20-02. Careful reading of a public domain report by RPS on the Lancaster field demonstrates up to 25m of weathered carapace to be present across the crest of the field. Fracture porosity within the carapace is estimated to be ca 3%, by analogy with other basement reservoirs worldwide. Lancaster also
shows fracturing associated with a fault which offsets top basement, with fractures extending locally deeper into the basement (205/21a-4/4z) generating a fracture corridor which probably extends over a depth interval of ca 150m into the basement. The width of this is unknown, but in the current volumetric assessment this is interpreted to be ca 20m wide, by analogy with outcrops of faulted basement on the Isle of Lewis. Maximum fracture porosity within fracture corridors is estimated as ca 6% by analogy with other reservoirs worldwide.

A volumetric uncertainty workflow has been used that combines the Low, Mid and High inputs of 7 key independent volumetric elements (top structure, isochore thickness, zonation style, sand facies, porosity, N:G and OWC). Each of the elements are combined in the  workflow to create 1458 models. The elements are given probabilities and the probabilities for each model case are cross multiplied to create a model case probability. This model probability has been used to define the Low (P90), Mid (P50) and High (P10) Cases. Note that a Low case does not necessarily include all low case elements. Similarly the high case does not necessarily include all high case elements.
